transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-30 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Carlos Medina (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Mosaic Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Zoe Park (NLP)

00:00 Carlos: ok welcome everyone, thanks for joining, this is Carlos from Redwood, we have Priya from the SE team, how are you all?
00:34 Maya: hey thanks, yeah doing well — excited to talk model selection, we've got a few constraints to run through.
01:10 Priya: quick agenda, we'll ask about current stack and production goals, walk through model options (context lengths, multilingual, tool-calling), then talk hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private) and next steps. sound good?
02:05 Liam: yep, we have three main workloads: long document summarization for research (docs up to ~200k tokens), a multilingual assistant (EN/FR/ES/DE/JP) and an agent workflow that calls internal APIs and external tools. latency target varies, but 200-400ms token latency preferred for interactive parts.
05:12 Priya: ok so two quick axes — context length and tool-calling. for context length, Redwood supports variants of open models and the runtime optimizes kv cache and continuous batching; we typically map longer-context variants for dedicated/private. do you expect 200k to be 1-off long queries or steady stream?
08:30 Maya: a mix, research will do big one-off doc ingests then chunked Q&A; the assistant needs persistent convo state of ~64k tokens sometimes, and the agent will have short context but needs reliable tool integration.
12:00 Carlos: got it. for model families we're seeing customers mix: Llama-derived 70B/13B quantized for cost, Mistral-like models for instruction, and some very long-context variants (we've seen up to 1M tokens in custom builds). folks often ask about tradeoffs: quality vs cost vs latency.
15:30 Zoe: can you clarify tool-calling? we have internal CRM and a payments API, plus a vector store. do you support function calling and safe isolation?
20:00 Priya: yes function/tool calling is supported in the hosted API; you can register schemas for tools and Redwood will stream calls and responses. on Dedicated/Private you get more control over network egress and can keep tool endpoints inside VPC. note: sometimes transcription shows 'tool calling' as tool-calling or toolcall — apologies if the export is messy.
25:00 Liam: security is huge for us. SOC 2 attested? KMS/HSM for keys? audit logs and SSO?
30:00 Carlos: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, supports customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated, audit logs in Console, and SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning. for Hosted we offer enterprise SSO and encrypted data at rest; long-term retention policies can be configured.
36:00 Maya: model selection: we need strong multilingual performance out of the box, not just English. any benchmarks on FR/ES/JP?
42:00 Priya: yes we run multilingual evals and can share per-model performance profiles. often non-English quality favors certain families (some open Mistral variants or LLaMA-derivs with multilingual pretraining). we recommend running a small eval on your sample corpus — we'll do that in the benchmark.
47:15 Zoe: curious about cost modelling — how do we compare hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved capacity for our usage profile?
48:00 Carlos: wrap up — we'll send a pricing sheet with per-token hosted numbers and dedicated commit tiers, plus a benchmark plan. next call we'll review benchmark results and dig into Private deployment requirements if needed. thanks everyone.
